newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-BALTA HOPES SHARES WILL REACH 2.5/3 LATS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-BALTA HOPES SHARES WILL REACH 2.5/3 LATS.

text.p: Insurance company Balta said that it hopes it shares would reach 2.5 to three lats by the end of the year after it joins the bourse at 1.75 lats.
The company said it intends to apply for a bourse listing after August 22 when it has finished placing its shares with investors.
"We hope that Balta's share price on the bourse would reach 2.5 to three (times its) nominal value," Andris Laizans, president of the company told a news conference.
The nominal value of Balta's share is one lats.
"Balta plans to pay in dividends of four to 10 percent of the nominal value in 1997," Laizans said.
The company also confirmed that it would apply for the bourse's official list.

If its application is accepted, Balta would be the first Latvian stock company to go public following a shareholders' decision. All of the other stocks on the Riga bourse have been listed in the process of privatisation.
Balta posted a first quarter profit of 282,341 lats against 423,000 lats for all of 1996 and 12 percent was paid in cash dividends.
The company is the local market leader in vehicle, agriculture and real estate insurance.
Balta registered some 700,000 lats in vehicle insurance premiums in June. It earlier said that it eyes half of the 10 million lat mandatory vehicle incurance market.
Balta is the biggest insurance company in the Baltic states by way of paid statutory capital of 3.2 million lats.
The central depository on Wednesday said it registered 1.19 million Balta shares.
